findings.summary: Stale doc comment: the HarvestDeps.ingestMaterial docstring still says the dep itself owns the maxClues cap, but the cap authority was moved to harvestCard (src/harvest.ts:521-527) and the assembly deliberately no longer caps a second time.

Write-budget accounting drift: a new transcript costs two bus writes (publishDoc on research:content + the content-clue on the board) but only one unit is reserved in `needed` and one consumed. Not covered by any spec criterion and it cannot under-publish a card, but --max-writes can be exceeded by up to one write per newly transcribed material.

D7 in the shipped path: the production-assembly concurrency test cannot distinguish the injected shared mutex from harvest's sequential for-loop (both hold in-flight at 1). The mutex semantics themselves are covered only by the ingestBatch unit test. Acceptable as combined coverage, but the starred production assertion is not by itself discriminative for the mutex.

Acceptance criteria 1 (npm ci / typecheck / test green twice) and 13-14 (live-machine e0-regression and real MinerU image ingest) are outside a read-only review; this verdict rests on the product code and test structure, with those criteria attested by the acceptance command results and the dispatcher's live runs.
